subject: evs
verifiedAgainst: NCERT textbook listing (ncert.nic.in/textbook.php) + table of contents in the book prelims PDF
note: Listed by NCERT under the subject "The World Around Us" (spelt "Our Wonderous World" in the dropdown).

topics.title: Living as a community
outcomes: Learner can describe how people in a locality work and celebrate together
misconceptions: Thinks a community means only one’s family
hooks: Van Mahotsav tree planting in the colony

topics.title: Ways of communicating
outcomes: Learner can compare ways people communicate (talking, letters, phone, signs)
misconceptions: Believes communication needs words only
hooks: Sign language and gestures at a crowded station

topics.title: Places and services in a neighbourhood
outcomes: Learner can identify public places (post office, bank, hospital) and what they do
misconceptions: Thinks a bank is just a place that keeps money in a safe
hooks: Map your gali: kirana, chemist, post office

topics.title: Money and saving
outcomes: Learner can explain why people save money and where
misconceptions: Believes money in the bank stays in a box with your name
hooks: A gullak vs a savings account

topics.title: Observing plants and animals closely
outcomes: Learner can observe and record features like beaks, feet and leaf shapes and link them to how organisms live
misconceptions: Thinks all birds eat the same food
hooks: Beaks of a parrot, kingfisher and sparrow

topics.title: Who eats what
outcomes: Learner can describe simple food relationships in a garden or forest
misconceptions: Believes only big animals are important in nature
hooks: Grasshopper, frog, snake on a farm

topics.title: Traditional ways of living with nature
outcomes: Learner can give examples of local knowledge and practices that protect plants and animals
misconceptions: Thinks traditional practices have nothing to teach science
hooks: Sacred groves; the Bishnoi community protecting trees

topics.title: Plants we use
outcomes: Learner can list uses of plants for food, medicine, shelter and craft
misconceptions: Believes medicines only come from factories
hooks: Neem twigs as datun; banana leaves as plates

topics.title: Healthy plate and balanced food
outcomes: Learner can group foods by what they do for the body and plan a balanced meal
misconceptions: Thinks food that tastes good is always healthy
Believes fat in food is always bad
hooks: Plan a thali with dal, roti, sabzi, curd and salad

topics.title: Junk food and tastes
outcomes: Learner can identify junk food and explain why it should be eaten rarely
misconceptions: Believes packaged juice is the same as fresh fruit
hooks: Read the label on a chips packet

topics.title: Sleep, play and feelings
outcomes: Learner can describe how sleep, exercise and talking about feelings help well-being
misconceptions: Thinks feeling sad means something is wrong with you
hooks: A "how I feel today" chart

topics.title: Journey of food from farm to plate
outcomes: Learner can trace the steps grains go through to reach the plate and avoid wasting food
misconceptions: Believes leftover food has no value
hooks: Wheat from the field to the chakki to the roti

topics.title: Floating and sinking
outcomes: Learner can predict and test which objects float or sink and make a boat that floats
misconceptions: Thinks heavy things always sink and light things always float
hooks: Why does a big iron ship float but an iron nail sink?

topics.title: Spinners and moving toys
outcomes: Learner can make a paper spinner and explain what makes it turn faster or slower
misconceptions: Believes things move on their own without a push or pull
hooks: Phirki at the mela

topics.title: Making and recycling paper
outcomes: Learner can describe how paper is made from plants and recycle paper in class
misconceptions: Thinks paper grows like leaves
hooks: Make recycled paper from old newspapers

topics.title: Natural and human-made materials
outcomes: Learner can classify materials as natural or human-made
misconceptions: Believes plastic is natural because it comes from oil
hooks: Compare a jute bag with a plastic bag

topics.title: Mountains, deserts, plains and coasts
outcomes: Learner can compare food, houses and clothes of people in different regions of India and link them to climate
misconceptions: Thinks deserts are always hot
hooks: Ladakh cold desert vs Thar desert

topics.title: Houses suited to the land
outcomes: Learner can explain why houses are built differently in different regions
misconceptions: Believes everyone should live in the same type of house
hooks: Stilt houses in Assam; flat roofs in Rajasthan

topics.title: The Sun and shadows during the day
outcomes: Learner can observe how shadows change in length and direction during the day
misconceptions: Thinks shadows are made of darkness that comes out of objects
Believes the Sun moves around the Earth
hooks: Measure a stick’s shadow at 9 am, 12 noon and 3 pm

topics.title: The Moon’s changing shape
outcomes: Learner can record the Moon’s shape over a month and describe the pattern
misconceptions: Thinks the Moon actually changes its shape
hooks: Purnima and Amavasya on the calendar
